fields.label: When to open a CAPA
fields.text:
FSQM-009 Part 3. A CAPA is opened for: product already released or requiring hold, rework, downgrade or destruction; any critical-limit or CCP deviation; a critical complaint or one alleging illness, injury, foreign material or an undeclared allergen; any repeat within twelve months; any audit, certification body or regulatory finding; any inspection finding not corrected on the spot; any withdrawal or recall including a test; a presumptive positive or adverse environmental trend; a glass or brittle plastic breakage where product or a food-contact surface was exposed; or anything the SQF Practitioner judges to warrant one.

A routine non-conformance corrected on the spot is recorded on the form that found it and does not open a CAPA. When in doubt, open one.

fields.label: CAPA No.
fields.help: Year and next sequential number in that year. Numbers are never reused.

fields.label: Source record reference
fields.help: The complaint no., SCAR no., hold tag no., inspection date or audit reference. Write this CAPA number back onto that record.

fields.label: CAPA owner
fields.help: The one person accountable for this CAPA reaching closure.

fields.label: This is a repeat of an earlier non-conformance
Earlier CAPA no., if a repeat
fields.help: A repeat means the earlier correction was never followed by a corrective action. Say so in the investigation.

fields.label: What was observed
fields.help: What was seen, not what is assumed to have caused it.

fields.label: Product already released may be affected
fields.help: If Yes or Unknown, invoke the recall and withdrawal procedure now. It does not wait for this investigation to finish (FSQM-009 Part 4).

fields.label: Containment comes first
fields.text: Before anything is analysed, make the product safe. Hold and tag affected material on FRM-702, stop the process where it is still running, and isolate the area or equipment. Record it here before starting the investigation.

fields.label: Affected product held / tagged on FRM-702
Getting to a real root cause
fields.text:
"Operator error" and "training issue" are not root causes — they are where an investigation stopped. If an operator made an error, ask why the process let that error reach product undetected.

Answer both questions: why the control failed, and why it was not detected sooner. The second is usually where the real corrective action lies.

fields.label: Five Whys
fields.help: Not every chain runs to five. Stop when you reach a cause the site can act on.

fields.label: Other analysis used, if five whys was not adequate
fields.help: A recurring failure, or one with several contributing causes, needs a cause-and-effect (fishbone) analysis. Attach it to this entry.

fields.label: Why was it not detected sooner
Investigated by
fields.help: A person knowledgeable about the incident and, where practical, not the person whose work is under examination.

fields.label: Written against the cause
fields.text: Corrective action is what is done so this does not happen again. It addresses the root cause above, not the symptom. Every action carries a named owner and a due date — an action without both is not an action.

fields.label: Where else could this happen
fields.text: Preventive action asks where the same cause could produce a non-conformance that has not occurred yet — another line, another product, another shift, another supplier, another machine with the same failure mode. Where the answer is nowhere, record that as the answer.

fields.label: Documents, programs or specifications changed
fields.help: Name the document and the revision it moved to. The change is made under document control.

fields.label: Training required, and who received it
fields.help: Name the module. Assign it in the Team Portal.

fields.label: This change affects the site's ability to deliver safe food, so the applicable aspects of the SQF System were reviewed (2.5.4.4)
Doing the work is not verifying it
fields.text:
2.5.3.1 requires actions to be determined, implemented AND verified. A CAPA is not closed because the work was done; it is closed because someone checked that it worked.

Set the method and the date when the action is agreed, not after it is finished. The date must be at least one full cycle of whatever failed — verifying a monthly check after one week proves nothing.

fields.label: How effectiveness will be verified
fields.help: Re-inspect at the next GMP inspection; review the next N records or batches; re-test; re-audit the clause; watch the complaint category for a quarter.

fields.label: What the verification found
fields.help: If not effective, the CAPA is not closed. Either the root cause was wrong or the action was insufficient — the investigation resumes at Section 4 and this record of the failed verification stays.

fields.label: Verified by
fields.statement: I have checked that the actions above were effective, by the method stated.

fields.label: A CAPA closes only when all of these hold
fields.text: The correction is done and recorded; the root cause is documented; every corrective and preventive action is complete; effectiveness has been verified and signed; any affected document, program or record has been updated; and the disposition of any affected product is resolved.

fields.label: All corrective and preventive actions complete
Closure summary
fields.help: Where a CAPA is closed because it was unnecessary, that reason is recorded here. CAPAs are never deleted.

fields.label: Closed by (SQF Practitioner)
fields.statement: I confirm this corrective action is complete, verified and closed.

fields.label: Retention
fields.text: Retained a minimum of two years, or the shelf life of the affected product plus twelve months, whichever is longer. A CAPA relating to a withdrawal or recall is retained permanently (FSQM-009 Part 10).
